en: Keen-sensed even from a hidden place,
Sons of the white-capped Kyrgyz,
When an exceedingly hard trial came,
When it came grimly before a man,
The ruin that befell him,
The best one for making a bargain,
If a giant fell headlong,
His champion who struck him headlong,
If a roaring giant came,
The one who boldly faced him,
If a fearsome, ruinous foe came,
He would shout and fight fiercely.
For the white-capped Kyrgyz people,
I have traveled through torment,
He stood vast as a sea.
A judge of men who discerned from afar,
Unable to find what he sought,
With imposing bearing, he began to speak,
Raging like lightning,
Roaring like a lion,
My omen in the heavens,
My companion beside me through hardship,
My chooser of warriors when I gird myself,
A black blade surpassing every craftsman,
The one who crushed calamity,
You were the strength of a black eagle,
They settled in a comfortable place for livestock,
Meeting them, they became an ornament amid the dust,
He became one whose horse could not be taken.
Have you seen what I have seen?
Have you endured what I have endured?
His loose-flowing hair had become renowned,
He became famous among the people.
Honored, he appeared before the people.
If he is a hero belonging to the people,
If he is a friend worn at one’s belt,
Let us take them four at a time.
If an enemy has come to besiege us,
Whatever people they have come from,
If their three assaults carry venom,
If their hell is as large as a mountain,
Without letting the people and realm know,
Let us hold fast to the work of speech.
If the Kyrgyz remain in hardship,
Let us sacrifice at Kurmandat.
However many children came from Mayman,
Calling out to Ebegey and Köböy,
Whether enemy or foe,
Let us lie down upon the pillow.
If there are people for us in the saddle,
Let us learn this news.
In the name of the people’s hero,
We shall see the song of hell,
Let us examine the road if it appears.
From the Kyrgyz coat and the Kyrgyz people,
Without surrendering the secret of many pleas,
Let us face the blowing wind.
Let us learn how much belongs to the devil,
Whether enemy or foe,
Let us wish for him to tremble completely.
This is the wish of the mounted one.
Thus spoke the two friends,
Turning themselves about in the night.
He startled deer from the ravine.
Forty hunters served as his trackers,
The courser’s spear,
Making his gun thunder.
Unable to stop, he whetted his tongue,
Turning from the dark faith toward the light,
Toward the path of the true Muslim,
Zhelzhetpes had come to draw them there.
Speaking verses of God,
Making its mysteries plain,
Zhelzhetpes was about to speak,
From the road veiled in dust and mist,
Zhelzhetpes was about to turn back.
The wrathful ruler’s rank and power,
Zhelzhetpes was about to tell.
From the dark faith to the bright path,
Zhelzhetpes was about to lead them.
Chinese without, human within,
If he spoke again, the words returned,
Would he simply keep repeating them?
Saying, “As it was before,”
Ebegei leveled his spear,
Kogoi, the blue-maned lion,
Drew his bright, keen sword,
Then Zhelzhetpes,
Speaking softly but with force,
Began a measured speech of many parts,
At hearing it, the heart was divided,
Such was the fashion of each word he spoke.
He appeared like a lofty mountain.
Ebegey and Köböy, the two companions,
We are the ones left behind and unresolved,
We are a people who voice lament.
On the honored day that gave shelter,
If a thick tongue was thrust forth,
The struggle for the khanship shifted,
The hardship settled at the place of honor.
He suffered in the movement,
He was broken before the khan,
We were the yellow-faced strangers,
We stood in the burned darkness.
We were stars and Venus in the grave,
We wandered under accusation,
Fleeing the khan and seeing much,
Hero, we wander unable to find peace.
All the heroes of Beijing,
We saw what the beks had seen,
As the sun heated the earth and its life,
He took the lone one they had established,
Because of his wrathful nature,
We came out from the treasury and people,
Let us surrender the one who cries aloud,
We fled from his wrath.
The black Dungan became white,
Knowing unity and seeking the faith,
Ebegey and Köböy sought the word,
We escaped from the wrathful one,
There is a battlefield where the kalpak is offered,
The khan’s kalpak-wearing hero,
There is a region that stands watching.
He sent the one who cast his eye upon it,
May the errant soul be safe among you.
In God’s name, this is what we became,
May the dear hero forgive us.
May the four forms never waver,
May the sea-like host be exhausted.
When we lived in Kokon,
We were the ones who led the people,
We came from Kokon,
We did not devour your people,
We had seen the designs of Moscow.
Whatever day befell us,
We saw the enemy’s wrath,
Unable to withstand the cold wind,
Sickness pierced us to the marrow,
There was no remedy for our staggering,
Taking the relic into our midst,
With no solution left, we panicked,
Unable to find a place to sustain life,
We fled without finding rest.
When we lived in Kokon,
We were Kyrgyz wearing quilted coats,
We were pure people who fielded cannon,
With great courage when facing the enemy,
We had been khans for forty years.
Like a river flowing from the core,
We were blood against the enemy,
Like water scattered abroad,
We were souls under oppression,
The matter returned to its beginning,
If this affair falls upon our brow,
We will bow our necks to death.
We were humiliated by the empire,
Fleeing from God, we became desperate,
We became full from so much migration,
We now come before you.
From another crown and throne,
Who has not shaken and burned?
While the empire held power,
Who has not lived under confinement?
This is the affair in which we broke our pledge,
Saying Padishah Jeljetpes would come,
In truth, you did not become Kokon.
The people of this city,
When that khan still stood at their head,
A blue-gray steed with a sweeping tail,
We had defeated many and grown strong,
Our horses raced upon the open steppe,
We used to range across the mountains,
When fortune stood over our heads,
Even youths would answer us with words.
We are warriors who guard the people,
We are of Kalmak blood and lineage,
Beaten by the wrathful one,
We are wretches who fled the khagan.
We are a people of trusted companions,
Against the dark enemy outside,
We came with our arms opened wide.
We are fighters with dun-colored manes,
Binding bullets into our wounds,
We are poor men who have been wounded.
Ebegei and Kogoi, the two lions,
Dragging their tails, raising an uproar,
We are coursers that win the prize,
Even untrained, when loosed we took the wolf,
We are dark gyrfalcons.
We are heroes equal to you,
Having encountered the khan’s wrath,
Driven about, unable to find a resting place,
We are diminished men whose people are gone.
We have gone about saying, “Receive us,”
If you choose to break and take our fortune,
We are among the honored ones.
Turning from the dark path toward the light,
Guarding the world by a hair’s breadth,
We have been struck down by the khan’s wrath,
Led astray by dark belief,
Wandering without finding a people,
We are heroes who fled the khagan,
Ebegei and Kogoi, the two giants,
If you send us from the host, we are capable,
We will bring back his tulpar.
We are twelve heroic champions,
Breaking a horde and taking a horde,
We will move like a dark-maned stallion,
The blessed Ala-Too will not be clouded,
If we do not wait, we shall die.
Without seeing humiliation, hardship, or quarrel,
We shall return and see it from our camp.
If you accept us, blessed one,
If the enemy is a ruined soul,
We will serve as wings for you.
When I lived in Kokon,
The black Chinese settled in splendor,
I was khan over the black people,
In Talas I was padishah over the people,
In Chüy I was their horde,
Among the Jalal people I was their realm.
Pearl and coral, precious stones,
I alone wore them outwardly.
Asking about affairs among the Chinese,
I was a son who knew them,
Riding the cloud and cloaked in frost,
I was one of the heroes who roamed.
A true Kyrgyz man among the four,
A turn lasting six months,
Since then the Kyrgyz have not taken it.
We are becoming men,
My people remain without lawful union,
Before the khan, the eye of the horde,
Among the horde’s maidens,
As in former times last year,
In the city of conquest,
My ancestors gave birth to me.
Whatever kind of khan my ancestor was,
He was one who led the people.
Thus he did not scatter them,
What kind of man went to the Chinese,
Name the four of you before you go.
Let us give it exactly so.
He addressed these words to Ebegei.
Coming together, the seven consulted among themselves,
His mother and father had died,
He was raised from the treasury,
Saying he would become master of the mares,
Entrusting him to the judge of horses,
No living soul could catch the ant,
A great man called Kündö,
Who served his khan,
Had him tended for ten days.
Beginning with silver ingots,
Zhelzhetpes, the wind-swift pacer,
Saying the orphan had become a fine racer,
